paragraphs: Rav Huna bar Chinena—in several places bar Chanina—in Rav Sheshet’s time (I did not find it), and his son in Rav Pappa’s time. He himself was also in Rav Pappa’s time, for Pesachim 16a says that he told his son, “When you enter before Rav Pappa, raise this contradiction to him.” In Ketubbot 61a: Rav Huna said, “Rav Huna bar Chinena tested us: she says she will nurse and he says she will not nurse …; we resolved for him that she rises with him and does not descend.” Rav Huna said, “What verse? ‘She is married to a husband ….’” Rabbi Elazar said, “From here: ‘She was the mother of all living’—she was given for life.” End of quotation. This is very puzzling: Rav Huna died before Rav Yehudah (see his entry); Rava was born on the day Rav Yehudah died; Rava told his student Rav Pappa to explain to Rav Huna bar Chinena. How, then, did Rav Huna say that Rav Huna bar Chinena tested him like a teacher testing a student? Moreover, the language is puzzling: after Rav Huna bar Chinena tested him, “She says …,” and he resolved, “She rises with him,” how does “Rav Huna said, ‘What verse?’” fit? It should say briefly, “We resolved: she rises with him, for it is written, ‘She is married to a husband.’” I searched with lamps, but they gave me no light. Yet I labored and found in Yalkut, Genesis, remez 33, as follows: Rav Pappa said, “Rava tested us: she says she will nurse …; we resolved: she rises with him and does not descend with him. What verse? ‘She is married to a husband ….’” This greatly pleased me. The earlier authorities did not attend to it, and newer Talmud editions did not correct it. But what it concludes there, “Rabbi Elazar says, ‘From here: she was the mother …,’” requires examination, for Rabbi Elazar preceded Rava. Rosh’s reading, “Rav Pappa said: Rav Huna bar Chinena tested us,” is also incorrect. Abaye, Rav Safra, and Rav Acha son of Rav Huna: Bava Batra 167b. Rav Huna son of Rav Nachman; they disagree with Rava: Avodah Zarah 57b; see there. He told his son, “When you enter before Rabbi Zerika, ask him”: Pesachim 73a. He reported Rav Chiyya bar Rav: Berakhot 30a. Rav Chiyya bar Avin told him, “You have spoken well”: Berakhot, there. He sat before Rav Chisda: Moed Katan 10b. He said to Rav Yosef: Eruvin 14b. He reported Rav Nachman: Ketubbot 100a; Kiddushin 42, end of side a; Avodah Zarah 24a; Temurah 30b; Bava Batra 155a. He thought to expound it in his lecture; Rava said to him …: Nedarim 23b. He said to Rava, “Explain it to me.” Rava told Rav Pappa, “Go and explain it to him”: Sanhedrin 87a. Rava’s shofar sounded to forbid, and Rav Huna bar Chinena’s shofar to permit …. Rabbi Yirmeyah of Difti said, “Rav Pappi told me personally: when Rav Huna bar Chinena permitted …”: Avodah Zarah 40a. He objects to Rava: Niddah 46a. Rava said to him, “One who does not know …”: Eruvin 67b. The exilarch told him to prepare a place to sit on the Sabbath in his orchard. Rava pulled them out; Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua; Ravina raised an objection to Rava. R.B. [ר״ב] applied to them, “They are wise to do evil, but to do good they do not know”: there, 26a. Rachava explained them: there, side b. And bar Tachlifa bar Immi sat before Rabbi Lazar.
